text:
alex: Heads-up — hitting a weird auth refresh + streaming cancel combo on Android 12 emulator with Retrofit 2.9 + OkHttp 4.11. Stream starts, then we get duplicated token refresh requests and the body closes mid-stream.
jamie: ugh that sounds like the authenticator getting called multiple times because of transparent retries? any logs?
alex: yup. Logs show two parallel requests to /auth/refresh within ~100ms. Server returns 200 then the original streaming call throws `java.io.IOException: stream closed` right after the second refresh completes.
maria: are you using an Authenticator or an Interceptor for refresh? Interceptor runs once, authenticator can be invoked by the client while a call is in-flight.
alex: Authenticator. We used it to get fresh tokens when 401. Also using coroutines with Dispatcher.IO + `suspend` network method via Retrofit adapter.
drew: coroutine cancellation can close the response body; combined with OkHttp retry it might spawn another attempt that triggers authenticator again. Could be a race.
jamie: can you paste the small repro snippet?
alex: sure — minimal flow:
```kotlin
interface Api { @GET("/stream") suspend fun stream(): Response<ResponseBody> }
// Retrofit + OkHttp client with Authenticator that does sync refresh via HttpUrl
```

alex: authenticator code basically does synchronized token refresh (we tried a mutex) but still saw duplicates on emulator.
maria: did you try disabling retry on connection failure? `okHttpClient.retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` — sometimes retry will do a second request before mutex state is visible.
alex: tried that, no dice. But toggling `authenticator` -> `interceptor` for attaching token eliminated duplicate refreshes because interceptor runs earlier and is single-threaded per call. However we rely on 401->refresh flow so that complicates it.
drew: interesting. For streaming endpoints you might not want OkHttp to replay the request: `RequestBody` can't be replayed if streaming. OkHttp will avoid retrying non-repeatable bodies but maybe response streaming + cancel triggers a reconnect path.
jamie: also check connectionPool eviction + keepalive; emulator networking quirks on Android 12 sometimes close sockets and produce an auth race.
alex: repro steps I've added to the sampleapp: run emulator API 31, start stream endpoint (server prints when /auth/refresh is called), call app stream button. I can share a log where you see `REFRESH START` x2 then `STREAM CLOSED` x1.
maria: can you try returning null from `Authenticator.authenticate` when the call has a streaming body? That signals no retry. Something like: `if (originalRequest.body is SomeStreamingMarker) return null`
alex: good idea. We also considered returning the same request without credentials as a signal to fail, but null is clearer.
drew: another safe pattern: make refresh endpoint idempotent and cheap, and guard refresh with a process-wide singleflight (or Kotlin `Mutex` + volatile token) so duplicates are harmless.
jamie: for DX note — our Android quickstart sample doesn't mention `retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` or the Authenticator vs Interceptor nuance for streaming. We should add a short section: "Streaming endpoints + Auth: prefer interceptor for token attach; if using 401-based refresh, ensure singleflight and consider disabling transparent retries for streams."
alex: filing a tiny doc PR for the sample app README and a new test case in the sampleapp to reproduce. Also attaching a small stack dump to the issue.
ci-bot: build/sampleapp-android #482 completed — artifact uploaded to //artifacts/sampleapp/1959993210/repro.apk :white_check_mark:
maria: thanks — once PR is up I can try proposed `return null` patch and run on Pixel 3 emulator.
jamie: if that works we should add a short note in devex channel and a one-line comment in sdk code about why we prefer interceptors or returning null for streaming calls.
alex: will do. PR coming in ~30m. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
